name: Alexander I of Yugoslavia
role: Regent of Serbia and the South Slav kingdom (1914–1921); king (1921–1934)
summary: Alexander promoted a centralized Yugoslav national identity and imposed royal dictatorship in 1929, later retaining extensive royal powers under his 1931 constitution. He supported peasant land redistribution and sought security through France, the Little Entente and Balkan cooperation.

notes:
Reviewed regency, wartime and royal periods, including the January dictatorship, censorship, agrarian reform, ethnic centralism and alliances. The 1918 proclamation and 1931 constitution were downloaded in full and searched; the 1929 proclamation was read online after direct fetching was blocked. Constitutional answers concern the personal regime he imposed, not incidental assent to ministers’ legislation. Other provisions, including welfare and religious guarantees, were not automatically attributed to him. Targeted searches on economy, religion, ecology and technology found no additional exact matches; all 490 statements and remaining nulls reviewed. No inferred answers. Auditor identification: the runtime identifies this assistant as GPT-6/Codex but does not expose an exact version or variant; gpt-6 is the available identifier, not an asserted variant.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 22 answers taken from it, 20 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (a first audit by another model exists). Evidence is his own 1918 proclamation, the 6 January 1929 proclamation and decrees, the 1931 proclamation and constitution, and the 1933 Rudnik speech, plus a reference work and a 1926 Britannica article. Constitutional answers rest on the 1931 constitution because he personally granted it and the proclamation says so; provisions that look like inherited practice (sharia courts for Muslim family law, the deferral of women's suffrage) are answered low or medium. Searched without finding his own words: economy (taxes, welfare, trade), world affairs and alliances (no speech or letter on the Little Entente or France was found as full text), religion beyond the constitution, ecology, technology. The 1929 church laws (Serbian Orthodox, Islamic, Jewish) were read but not used: they were proposed by the justice minister and show no position of his own. No source found for the banning of trade unions, the press laws, the 1929 renaming of the state or the banovina reform beyond the constitution text, so those are null. Answers resting on what his regime did rather than on his words: suppress-opposition, decide-locally, regional-powers-revocable, minority-territorial-autonomy, women-suffrage, uniform-civil-code.
